I've farmed this land 40 years, and with my high school schooling I keep up with what the agri-tech station and dealers in Quzhou tell us. My 12 mu runs the standard wheat-maize double crop — winter wheat October to June, summer maize June to early October. Well irrigation means I don't gamble on rain.

For wheat, I'll plant Jimai 22 or Shixin 828, improved varieties — my neighbors got 500 kg/mu with them last year. Basal fertilizer before sowing: one bag of diammonium (50 jin ≈ 25 kg, giving about 4.5 kg P and 8 kg N) plus 15 kg of compound 15-15-15 per mu, then top-dress 15 kg urea at jointing. That puts me around 17 kg N, 7 kg P, 5 kg K per mu. Wheat needs 3 waterings here — winter water in December, jointing water in March, and filling water in May. Two sprays: one for aphids and powdery mildew at booting, one combined herbicide earlier. I rotary till after maize harvest because straw return works better that way.

For summer maize I'll use Zhengdan 958 or a similar hybrid, direct drilled no-till into the wheat stubble to save time — I only have about a week between harvests. Base fertilizer 20 kg compound plus side-dress 20 kg urea at big trumpet stage, plus 10 kg potassium sulfate. About 19 kg N, 6 kg P, 7 kg K. Two waterings usually enough — after sowing if dry, and at tasseling. One spray for corn borer, plus a pre-emergence herbicide. Maize target 600 kg/mu, wheat 500 kg/mu. I'd rather spend the extra 30-40 yuan on urea than watch yellow leaves in June — a lost harvest would cost me thousands.
